newsitem.title: UK: Philippines says it amends terms of Brady exchange.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says it amends terms of Brady exchange.

text.p: The Republic of the Philippines has amended the terms under which it will accept offers to exchange $1.9 billion of defaulted debt bonds into new uncollateralised bonds, the Philippines said in a statement.
Originally all offers to exchange 2017 or 2018 bonds for fixed or floating rate bonds would be rejected if the acceptance would result in the issue of less than $200 million of bonds.

"This provision will be amended to grant persons who have submitted noncompetitive offers to exchange 2017 and/or 2018 bonds for a series of new bonds and whose offers would otherwise have been rejected because the minimum aggregate principal amount of $200 million for such series of new bonds has not been reached the option to exchange the 2017 and/or 2018 bonds originally tendered for the other series of new bonds instead at the applicable exchange values," the Philippines said.
The Philippines deal follows a path set by Mexico, the first to use the so-called Brady plan to restructure defaulted commercial debt in 1989 and in April, the first to swap Bradys for new bonds.
It removes the use of U.S. Treasuries as collateral for the paper and allows yield-hungry investors to obtain straight exposure to the economy and their high- yielding assets.

Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co. has assigned a 'BB' (Double-B) rating to the forthcoming Philippines global bonds, which are being issued in exchange for the Philippines' Brady Par Bonds, Series A and B.
The government is offering 15-year floating rate bonds and 20-year fixed rate bonds, with interest yields to be fixed on September 18.
The series A Brady bonds, which have an outstanding $413 million, will mature in the year 2018. The series B, which have an outstanding $1.7 billion, will mature in 2017.
The invitation to tender the Brady bonds began on September 2 and expires on September 20. Acceptance of offers will be announced on September 20 and settlement made on October 7.
J.P. Morgan is arranger of the new issues.
